panels.title: Health — is the pipeline OK at 3am?
Flink scrape targets up
panels.description: Number of Flink Prometheus endpoints (JobManager + TaskManager) Prometheus is successfully scraping. 0 means metrics are blind.

panels.title: Job restarts (per window)
panels.description: Full restarts of the userKeys streaming job within the selected time range (windowed increase of the cumulative counter). A flat 0 is healthy; a step shows exactly when a restart occurred so it can be correlated with load or checkpoint events.

panels.title: Failed checkpoints (per window)
panels.description: Checkpoints that failed within the selected time range (windowed increase). 0 during healthy operation; the benign one-time startup trigger-abort drops out because the lifetime counter stays flat. A nonzero step means checkpoints are failing now and is correlatable in time.

panels.title: Last checkpoint duration
panels.description: Duration of the most recent checkpoint over time (auto-scaled: ms for fast checkpoints, s for slow ones). A flat low line is healthy; a trend toward the 60s checkpoint timeout indicates backpressure or a slow write path.

panels.title: Last checkpoint size
panels.description: On-disk size of the most recent completed checkpoint for the userKeys job. The state is the open tumbling-window accumulators (per (user_id, key) running sum), so size tracks the number of distinct keys in flight; a steady climb that never drops back after windows fire points at unbounded key growth.

panels.title: Kafka consumer lag — committed (Kafka) vs pending (Flink)
panels.description: Two views of how far behind ingest the userKeys pipeline is, on one axis so the gap is visible. 'committed lag (Kafka)' = latest - committed offset from kafka-exporter for consumer group flink-userkeys-processor on the user-keys topic; Flink commits offsets only on a successful checkpoint, so this is the authoritative durable-progress signal and matches Kafka UI. 'pending records (Flink)' = latest - in-flight read position from Flink's own gauge, reported only while the source task is RUNNING. Healthy: both small, committed riding slightly above pending in a checkpoint-interval sawtooth. A widening gap (committed climbing while pending stays low or goes stale) means checkpoints are not completing, so offsets stop committing — the canonical 'are we keeping up' alarm, hence Health not Throughput.

panels.title: DLQ records / sec by stage
panels.description: Rate of dead-letter records emitted, broken down by the originating pipeline stage. The userKeys job dead-letters only at the parse stage (PARSE), so a single series is expected; sink-side permanent failures surface as checkpoint/job failures and a restart loop, not DLQ routing. Backed by the custom dlq_records counter on the dlq-meter operator.

panels.title: Backpressure & busy time (ms/s per task)
panels.description: Per-task time spent backpressured vs busy for the userKeys job. Backpressure approaching 1000 ms/s means a downstream operator (the XA Postgres sink) is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Throughput & performance — workload shape, not paging signals
Kafka consumer lag — committed (Kafka) vs pending (Flink)
panels.description: Mirror of the Health-row lag panel, stacked directly above records/sec so lag can be cross-referenced against throughput without leaving the Throughput view: rising committed lag while records/sec is flat means the pipeline, not the inbound rate, is the bottleneck. Both series (committed lag from kafka-exporter, pending records from Flink) share the Health-row panel's meaning; the paging-grade copy lives in the Health row.

panels.title: Aggregate rows produced / sec
panels.description: Per-second rate of window-result rows entering the Postgres write operator (user_key_agg_to_postgres). Reporter-native numRecordsIn, no custom code. One row per closed (user_id, key) tumbling window, so this is window-firing throughput, not the inbound event rate. Physical persistence is batched: the XA sink commits one transaction per checkpoint, so these rows reach Postgres in checkpoint-sized batches rather than continuously.

panels.title: Cumulative aggregate rows written
panels.description: Running total of window-aggregate rows entering the Postgres write operator since the job started. Same numRecordsIn series as aggregate rows/sec (to the left), shown as the raw counter for the long-run row volume. Resets to 0 on a job restart (expected).
